results.name: Band Prone Incline Hammer Curl
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, with your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability. Hold the handles of a resistance band anchored below the bench, with your arms fully extended down and palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Curl the handles of the band upwards towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and your palms facing each other throughout the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your arms back down towards the floor.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary and close to your body to maximize biceps engagement.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
results.description: Band Prone Incline Hammer Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Band Reverse Spider Curl
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold the ends of a resistance band anchored below the bench, with your arms extended downward and palms facing back (pronated grip).
Curl the handles of the band upwards towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your arms back down towards the floor.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary to maximize biceps engagement.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
results.description: Band Reverse Spider Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Alternate Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with one hand, your palm facing forward (supinated grip). Keep your arm fully extended by your side.
Keep your elbow close to your torso. Slowly curl the barbell up towards your shoulder, maintaining the supinated grip with your palm facing upward.
Squeeze your bicep at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbow stays stationary and close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
Visualize the bicep contraction to enhance the mind-muscle connection for better results.
Ensure your movements are symmetrical to avoid muscle imbalances; focus equally on both arms.
results.description: Barbell Alternate Biceps Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Biceps Curl Close Grip
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using a close supinated grip (palms facing forward). Your hands should be closer than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, maintaining the supinated grip with your palms facing upward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows stay stationary and close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
Visualize the bicep contraction to enhance the mind-muscle connection for better results.
results.description: Barbell Biceps Curl Close Grip is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a normal grip (hands positioned at shoulder-width apart) and palms facing up.
Curl the barbell upward towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, focusing on engaging your biceps.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches shoulder height.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary and close to your body throughout the movement.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell.
Exhale as you curl the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.

results.name: Barbell Drag Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using a supinated grip (palms facing up). Your hands should be about shoulder-width apart.
Begin by pulling your elbows back and curling the barbell up along your body, dragging it against your torso.
Continue to pull the barbell upward until it reaches chest level, keeping your elbows back and close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control and keeping the barbell close to your torso. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows back to ensure the barbell stays close to your torso throughout the movement.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
results.description: Barbell Drag Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Lap Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with palms facing up, shoulder-width apart. Rest the bar on your thighs, just above your knees.
Begin the curl by bending your elbows and lifting the barbell towards your chest, keeping your upper arms stationary against your sides.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to your chest.
Lower the barbell back to your thighs with control. Just before touching your thighs, repeat the curl.
tips: Keep your elbows fixed on your thighs to isolate your biceps effectively.
Avoid using momentum by performing the movement slowly and with control.
Use a weight that allows for proper form to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell Lap Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Biceps Curl Cable Wide Grip
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing a low cable pulley. Hold the handle attached to the low pulley with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands just wider than shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended and elbows close to your body.
Curl the handle upwards towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning back during the curl.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
results.description: Biceps Curl Cable Wide Grip is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
